name: Updating Two-Dimensional List (Case 3)
description: Construct a program that initializes a 2x4 two-dimensional matrix that has multiples of 10 from 10 to 80 for entries, updates the last row to a list holding values 1,3,5,7, then sets the second element of the first row to be 8, and finally prints the matrix.
code:
#Step 1: Define a 2x4 two-dimensional list 
matrix = [[ 10, 20, 30, 40 ],
          [ 50, 60, 70, 80 ]]
#Step 2: Update the two-dimensional list 
matrix[1] = [1, 3, 5, 7]
matrix[0][1] = 8
#Step 3: Print the list
print(matrix)

commentList: We need to use two-dimensional list (a list of lists) to create a matrix. Each matrix row corresponds to a sublist in the two-dimensional list. This statement creates a 2x4 two-dimensional list called matrix and initializes its entries with multiples of 10 from 10 to 80.
Note that lists can naturally span multiple lines if we want them to because they are contained by a pair of brackets.
This statement assigns a list holding values 1,3,5,7 to the last row of the matrix.

In a two-dimensional list, we can get an entire matrix row (a nested sublist) by using one index. The row index could start at 0 and continue up to but not including the length of the two-dimensional list, i.e., the number of rows in the two-dimensional list.

In this statement, the list on the right-hand side of the assignment operator is the new list that we want to assign to the matrix row. The index of the last row in the matrix is 1. So, matrix[1] corresponds to the last row in the matrix.
This statement sets the second element of the first row in the matrix to be 8.

In a two-dimensional list, we can access an element within a matrix row (a nested sublist) by using two indices. The first index in [] is the row index and the second index in [] is the column index. The row index could start at 0 and continue up to but not including the length of the two-dimensional list, i.e., the number of rows in the two-dimensional list. The column index could start at 0 and continue up to but not including the length of the row, i.e., the number of elements within the row.
The second element of the first row in the matrix has the row index of 0 and the column index of 1. So, matrix[0][1] corresponds to the second element in the first row of the matrix.
We can see the content of the two-dimensional list by calling the print function and passing the two-dimensional list to that. This statement will print the entire matrix.
